profile_text.body:
Arm is a public company founded in 1990 and headquartered in Cambridge, United Kingdom. On its website, Arm describes itself as providing compute platforms behind advanced AI, from cloud to edge, trusted by innovators worldwide. The company says its compute platform connects cloud, edge, and physical AI with consistent software, flexible compute, and an ecosystem built to scale intelligence everywhere.

Arm's AI offerings include the Arm AI Portal, which gives developers and agents one place to discover optimized models, evaluate performance, access deployment workflows, or optimize their own models for Arm. The company states it delivers performance, efficiency, and flexibility for cloud, personal devices, AI-defined vehicles, and robotics. It highlights an AGI CPU launch and describes agentic AI as reshaping data centers, with efficiency becoming the defining metric for the AI era. Arm also positions itself in edge AI, saying it delivers real-time, private, power-efficient compute across consumer and embedded devices, and scalable, energy-efficient compute for autonomous machines. The site notes that NVIDIA DGX Spark, built on Arm-based NVIDIA Grace Blackwell technology, brings high-performance AI computing to developers' desktops.

No lawsuits are listed for Arm in the available records, and no products are tracked.
